etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle French invasion, from Late Latin invāsiōnem, accusative of invāsiō.

definitions.definition: A military action consisting of armed forces of one geopolitical entity entering territory controlled by another such entity, generally with the objective of conquering territory or altering the established government.

quote.text: Since Michel's days, however, many barbarian invasions had subdivided the Three Gauls into a melange of warsome states and tribes, all, nevertheless, acquiring a vaguely similar grace, if not a petite grandeur.

quote.citation: 2022 July 7, “Inspired by Ukraine, civilians study urban warfare in Taiwan”, in France 24‎[1], archived from the original on 07 July 2022‎[2]:
quote.text: Yeh actually works in marketing, and his weapon is a replica -- but he is spending the weekend attending an urban warfare workshop to prepare for what he sees as the very real threat of a Chinese invasion.

definitions.definition: The entry without consent of an individual or group into an area where they are not wanted.
(medicine) The spread of cancer cells, bacteria and such to the organism.

quote.citation: 2015 September 8, Filomena Cetani et al., “A nonfunctioning parathyroid carcinoma misdiagnosed as a follicular thyroid nodule”, in World Journal of Surgical Oncology‎[3], volume 13, →DOI:
quote.text: The histological diagnosis of PC is currently restricted to lesions showing unequivocal extra-parathyroidal growth, as evidenced by perineural invasion, full thickness capsular invasion with growth into adjacent tissues, extratumoral vascular invasion, or metastasis.

definitions.definition: (surgery) The breaching of the skin barrier.
